_about: Dated anchor towns for Soviet capture of German Reich territory outside 1939 Poland, 12 January – 8 May 1945 (see build-borders.py). `soviet` is the first day the place is shown as Soviet-held; null means German-held to the end of the map. Every place in Reich territory takes the date of its nearest anchor within `radiusKm` (default 100); beyond that it stays German, which includes areas taken by the Western Allies. Anchors marked `pocket` (Wrocław, Żuławy, the Vistula Spit) are circles of `radiusKm` that override their surroundings, because they held out longer. `by`, `approx` and `confidence: search-quote` as in the other anchor files.

anchors.name: Lwówek Śląski
anchors.note: From mid-February 1945 the front ran along the Lusatian Neisse and just north of Lwówek Śląski, Złotoryja and Strzelin, and held there until the capitulation, so this town and the mountains south of it stayed German.
